title.en: Host a guest, avoid the clash
title.es: Recibir a un invitado sin choques

es: Recibir a un invitado extranjero: explicar dos costumbres con matices, aclarar un malentendido con tacto y responder a una pregunta incómoda.

vocabulary.es: no quise decir, no era mi intención

teaching.en: Please feel at home, Carlos: the guest room is ready, and the bathroom is on the left.
teaching.es: Siéntete como en casa, Carlos: la habitación de invitados está lista y el baño está a la izquierda.
teaching.explanationEs: Feel at home es una bienvenida cálida; guest room es la habitación de invitados.
segments: Please feel at home, Carlos: the guest room is
ready, and the bathroom is on the left.
teaching.audioText: Please feel at home, Carlos: the guest room is ready, and the bathroom is on the left.

teaching.en: I apologise: I should have explained our custom about shoes.
teaching.es: Me disculpo: debería haberte explicado nuestra costumbre sobre los zapatos.
teaching.explanationEs: Apologise reconoce un fallo sin dramatizar; se dice apologise for…, no «apologise you».
teaching.audioText: I apologise: I should have explained our custom about shoes.

teaching.en: Let me clarify: we did not mean to be rude when we finished dinner early.
teaching.es: Déjame aclarar: no queríamos ser maleducados cuando terminamos de cenar pronto.
teaching.explanationEs: Clarify + we did not mean to… aclara la intención sin culpar a nadie.
segments: Let me clarify: we did not mean to
be rude when we finished dinner early.
teaching.audioText: Let me clarify: we did not mean to be rude when we finished dinner early.

teaching.en: That is an awkward question, but I will answer it honestly and tactfully.
teaching.es: Es una pregunta incómoda, pero la responderé con honestidad y con tacto.
teaching.explanationEs: Reconocer lo delicado y responder con tacto evita una discusión.
segments: That is an awkward question, but I
will answer it honestly and tactfully.
teaching.audioText: That is an awkward question, but I will answer it honestly and tactfully.

teaching.en: Good question! It is not awkward at all, and no offence taken.
teaching.es: ¡Buena pregunta! No es nada incómoda, y no me he ofendido.
teaching.explanationEs: Good question y no offence taken suavizan una pregunta delicada.
segments: Good question! It is not awkward
at all, and no offence taken.
teaching.audioText: Good question! It is not awkward at all, and no offence taken.

feedback.es: La fórmula de bienvenida es feel at home.

hint.es: Es el lugar donde uno se siente cómodo: feel at ___.

prompt.es: Elige la aclaración que no culpa al invitado.

choices.text: You should know that we wait; it is obvious.
You are rude because you started before us.
Let me clarify: in my family we wait until everybody sits down.

feedback.es: Let me clarify explica la costumbre sin acusar; las otras frases culpan al invitado.

hint.es: Busca la frase que explica la costumbre sin acusar.

origin.text: A guest starts eating before the family sits down. The host wants to clarify the custom.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me disculpo por no haberte explicado antes nuestra costumbre.»

answer.text: I apologise for not explaining our custom earlier

feedback.es: Apologise va con for y un verbo en -ing: apologise for not explaining.

hint.es: Empieza por I apologise y sigue con for + verbo en -ing.

prompt.es: Escucha a la anfitriona y elige qué hace.

choices.text: She apologises and offers an explanation.
She blames the guest for the problem.
She asks the guest to leave the table.

feedback.es: Pide disculpas con I am sorry, aclara la intención con I did not mean y ofrece explicar.

origin.audio: I am sorry. I did not mean to make you feel awkward. Let me explain why we eat so early.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta tactful a una pregunta incómoda del invitado.

choices.text: That is none of your business.
Good question! We tend to use it only on special days.
We never use it, and nobody asks.

feedback.es: Good question reconoce la pregunta y tend to matiza la respuesta; las otras son bruscas o absolutas.

origin.text: A guest asks, “Why do you not use the big table?” You do not want to offend him.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función al recibir a un invitado.

pairs.es: reconoce una pregunta delicada con calidez
dice que no me he ofendido

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función distinta en la conversación con el invitado.

prompt.es: Lee la respuesta del invitado y elige lo que probablemente significa.

choices.text: He will arrive early on Saturday.
He wants to bring his whole family.
He probably cannot come.

feedback.es: Might be a bit difficult y I will think about it, sin fecha, forman un rechazo cortés.

origin.text: The host invites her guest to a family party on Saturday. He answers, “That might be a bit difficult, but I will think about it.”

prompt.es: Corrige la generalización del texto para tu invitado con un matiz.

answer.text: By and large, families here tend to eat dinner at six
accepted: By and large, families here tend to eat dinner at six
As a rule, families here eat dinner at six
Families here tend to eat dinner around six

feedback.es: Un marcador como by and large o tend to convierte «todas» en una tendencia y evita el absoluto.

origin.text: All families here eat dinner at six.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige la causa del malentendido con el invitado.

choices.text: Carlos assumed that the time on the invitation was the real arrival time.
The family assumed that Carlos would cook.
Carlos assumed that dinner was cancelled.

feedback.es: Carlos dio por hecho que la hora de la invitación era la hora real; la familia esperaba que llegara más tarde.

origin.audio: The invitation said seven. Carlos arrived at seven, but the family was still cooking. In their country, guests usually arrive later than the time on the invitation.

prompt.es: Explica dos costumbres, aclara un malentendido y responde con tacto a tu invitado.

answer.text: Welcome, Carlos, and please feel at home! In my family we tend to eat dinner at six, and by and large everybody helps to set the table. Let me clarify something about last night: we did not mean to be rude when we started eating without you. I apologise, because I should have explained that we usually do not wait after seven. You asked a good question: why do we not talk more at dinner? Some families tend to be quieter, and ours likes to enjoy the food first. It is only a habit, and nobody is upset. Tomorrow we will talk as much as you like, and I will show you the city.
accepted: Welcome, Carlos, and please feel at home! In my family we tend to eat dinner at six, and by and large everybody helps to set the table. Let me clarify something about last night: we did not mean to be rude when we started eating without you. I apologise, because I should have explained that we usually do not wait after seven. You asked a good question: why do we not talk more at dinner? Some families tend to be quieter, and ours likes to enjoy the food first. It is only a habit, and nobody is upset. Tomorrow we will talk as much as you like, and I will show you the city.

Hello, Carlos, make yourself at home! As a rule, my family has breakfast together at eight, and we tend to be quiet because we are still sleepy. Let me explain something about this morning: we did not mean to ignore you. I am sorry, because I should have told you about our custom. That is a fair question: why is nobody talking? In some houses people talk a lot at breakfast, whereas in ours we like silence and coffee. It is only a habit, and nobody is angry. At lunch we will talk as much as you like, and I promise to ask you about your country.

feedback.es: El texto da la bienvenida, explica costumbres con matices, aclara el malentendido sin culpar y responde con tacto.

origin.text: Tu invitado Carlos llega de otro país. Escribe unas 80–140 palabras en inglés: da la bienvenida, explica dos costumbres con matices (tend to, by and large), aclara un malentendido (por ejemplo, que empezasteis a comer sin él) con Let me clarify… y responde con tacto a su pregunta: «Why do you not talk more at dinner?».

prompt.es: Elige la frase que pide disculpas y aclara sin culpar al invitado.

choices.text: You should have asked me earlier.
I apologise; I did not mean to upset you.
It is your fault, not mine.

feedback.es: Pedir disculpas y aclarar la intención tranquiliza al invitado; las otras frases lo culpan.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es una pregunta incómoda, pero te responderé con honestidad.»

feedback.es: Awkward describe una pregunta delicada o incómoda de responder.

She asks the guest to eat alone.

feedback.es: Aclara con Let me clarify, explica su costumbre con tend to y reconoce que debió avisar.

origin.audio: Let me clarify: we did not mean to ignore you. We tend to be quiet at breakfast, and I should have told you.
